name: Mawak
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3 languoid page mawa1266 (and ref 669906 World Oral Literature Project)
sources.note: Reference list only: Z'graggen 1968/1969/1971/1975/1980, Pick 2020/2022, Moseley 2010, Ethnologue, and a generic multi-language WOLP misc entry; no grammar/phonology/sketch doctype. AES: moribund.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2020. A reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert phonology and lexicon. PhD dissertation, University of Hawai'i at Manoa. 486 pp.
sources.note: sec. 1.5.1 pp. 31-32: stress described only for Mauwake (2nd syllable, Berghall 2015), Pamosu (Tupper 2012) and Usan (phonemic, Reesink 1987); 'the available data on stress in most languages are minimal or nonexistent'. sec. 3.5 Mawak pp. 124-125: consonant inventory /p t nd k ŋg m n f s h r w y/ from Z'graggen's wordlist only, 'tentative'; five vowels (p. 102); nothing on stress. p. 103: for Mawak the only data are Z'graggen's wordlist. sec. 9.2.6 pp. 363-364 sound changes; nothing on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1980. A comparative word list of the Northern Adelbert Range languages, Madang Province, Papua New Guinea. Pacific Linguistics D-31. Canberra: ANU. (Mawak = F9)
sources.note: Intro sec. 7 (p. ix): transcription 'semi-phonemic'; fluctuation table lists Mawak y ~ j; wordlist carries no stress marks; no statement on stress.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1975. The Madang-Adelbert Range Sub-Phylum. In S. A. Wurm (ed.), New Guinea Area Languages and Language Study 1, 569-612. Pacific Linguistics C-38.
sources.note: F9 Mawak (31 speakers) appears in population and pronoun tables; note that Mawak's geographical location was corrected; no mention of stress or tone.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District. Pacific Linguistics C-19. Canberra: ANU. (Mawak = language 28 / Mk)
sources.note: sec. 1.3.3 p. 6: 'The marking of stress has been omitted, since the stress patterning has not been well established yet.' sec. 2.22.23.11 p. 51: Mawak 'Previously unrecorded', 1,020 speakers, village list. sec. 2.22.23.3 p. 52 Mawamuan Family typology: /h/ in all members; /l/ and /r/ 'seem to be allophones' in Mawak; prenasalized voiced stops; nothing on stress. sec. 2.22.8 p. 73: 'None of the languages appears to be tonal' (Adelbert Range Phylum).

sources.citation: Z'graggen, John A. 1969. Classificatory and typological studies in languages of the Madang District, New Guinea. PhD thesis, Australian National University.http://hdl.handle.net/1885/130077
sources.note: p. 13 (PDF 22): identical stress-omission sentence; pp. 89-90: Mawamuan typology as in the 1971 book; nothing on Mawak stress. Thesis = the 1971 PL C-19 book.
Only source is Z'graggen (1980); retyped lexicon, no stress marks, no phonology.
Classification and speaker count only (25 speakers, 2000 census); cites Ethnologue and Pick 2020; no phonology.

sources.citation: Pick, Andrew. 2022. A Reconstruction of Proto-Northern Adelbert Phonology and Lexicon. In Epps, Law & Pat-El (eds.), Historical Linguistics and Endangered Languages: Exploring Diversity in Language Change, 215-262. Routledge.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Only other published work treating Mawak phonology; condensed from the 2020 dissertation, so almost certainly silent on Mawak stress, but should be checked to close the record.

sources.citation: Tupper, Ian. 2012. A grammar of Pamosu. PhD thesis, La Trobe University (cited by Pick 2020 as Tupper 2012: 99-102 for Pamosu stress).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Not Mawak, but the closest well-described Tibor relative (Pick 2020 p. 31: Pamosu stress mostly predictable, final on closed final syllables, antepenultimate on open final syllables); the only proxy for what a Mawak stress description might look like. Belongs under hini1240 [hih], not mawa1266.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, J. A. 1971b. Field recordings, Madang Province (PARADISEC collection JZ1).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.note: Pick 2020 p. 124 fn. 48 reports that no Mawak recording has been identified in the digitized collection (the file labelled 'Lg F09 Mawak' is Pamosu); audio, not a description; listed only so no one re-hunts it.

sources.citation: Z'graggen, Johannes. 1968. A Linguistic Survey of the Central North-East Coast of New Guinea. Anthropica (Gedenkschrift P. Wilhelm Schmidt), 421-428.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Earliest survey note on the area; 8 pages; very unlikely to state Mawak stress but not opened.
